cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Merciful Lie
cards.instruction: Choose a truth your character believes would hurt someone. Keep it from them, even as honesty becomes harder.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. The bakery can't sell your cake, love. They think it's too special to slice.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The letter says 'inedible.' I thought I'd finally found something I was good at.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. You have. Display cakes aren't meant to be eaten.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then I'll ask them to put it in the window.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me ask. I'll explain the display concept before they get confused again.

mechanism: A protects a baker from a painful verdict by authoritatively approving an alternative interpretation and controlling contact with the bakery.
confusable: Avoidance alone conceals a topic; this Drive needs a visibly protective motive and a hurtful truth A keeps reframing.
comparison: A rejected cake is reframed as display art with A mediating contact; a rejected poem asks A to publicly endorse the merciful interpretation.
seedUse: D15-a supplies inedible wording and vulnerable self-belief; S01 must make A comforting reinterpretation an authoritative ruling.
